manglik_dosha.name: Manglik / Kuja Dosha
manglik_dosha.rule: Mars in houses 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, or 12 from Lagna, Moon, or Venus.

source_refs.detail: Kuja/Manglik placement rules; exact verse pending

manglik_dosha.practitioner_explanation: Mars occupies one of six houses (1/2/4/7/8/12) counted from each of three reference points — Lagna, Moon, and Venus — independently. Raw severity scales with how many of the three references are affected (1=mild, 2=moderate, 3=strong). Widely-published exception rules (Mars in its own or exalted sign, Jupiter's graha drishti on Mars, Mars-Moon conjunction) apply a one-step downgrade to net_severity; the floor is 'mild' while any reference stays active, so an exception weakens but never fully erases an active flag by itself in this implementation.
manglik_dosha.lay_explanation: Mars sits in a handful of specific positions relative to your ascendant, Moon, or Venus — a placement traditionally checked before marriage matching, and often softened by other factors elsewhere in the same chart.
manglik_dosha.strength_rubric: severity: 1 active reference (of Lagna/Moon/Venus) = mild, 2 = moderate, 3 = strong. net_severity downgrades one step when any exception rule applies (see caveats), floored at mild while active.
caveats: Classical exception: Mars in its own sign (Aries or Scorpio) or exalted (Capricorn) weakens the dosha.
Classical exception: Jupiter's graha drishti (5th/7th/9th aspect) on Mars weakens the dosha.
Classical exception: Mars conjunct the Moon in the same sign weakens the dosha.
This is a flag, not a verdict — treat it as one input among many, never as a marriage veto by itself.
notes: Widely published exception rules (Mars own/exalted sign, Jupiter drishti on Mars, Mars-Moon conjunction) are applied as convention-dependent weakening factors in 'net_severity'; raw 'severity' is unchanged.
Use this as a deterministic flag, not a final marriage judgement.

gandanta_dosha.name: Gandanta Dosha
gandanta_dosha.rule: Moon, Lagna, or Sun within one pada (3°20') of a water→fire sign junction: Ashlesha–Magha (Cancer/Leo), Jyeshtha–Moola (Scorpio/Sagittarius), Revati–Ashwini (Pisces/Aries).

source_refs.detail: Rashi/nakshatra sandhi affliction; exact verse pending
One-pada zone width and 0°48'/1°40' severity bands follow the common software convention; golden-chart validation pending

gandanta_dosha.practitioner_explanation: Checks Moon, Lagna, and Sun for placement within one pada (3°20') of any of the three water→fire sign/nakshatra junctions. Severity grades by exact distance from the junction point: within 0°48' is severe, within 1°40' is moderate, otherwise mild (still within the one-pada zone).
gandanta_dosha.lay_explanation: One of your key chart points sits right at a sign changeover — a junction some traditions read as an ending running straight into a beginning, worth settling into gently rather than rushing.
gandanta_dosha.strength_rubric: severity by distance from the junction: <=0°48' severe, <=1°40' moderate, else mild (anywhere within the one-pada zone).
caveats: Jyeshtha–Moola gandanta (Abhukta Mula) is traditionally treated as the most intense of the three junctions.
Zone width (one pada each side) and the severity orbs are convention-dependent; some traditions size the Moon-vs-Lagna zones differently.
notes: Zone width (one pada on each side) and severity orbs are convention-dependent; some traditions use different spans for Moon vs Lagna.
Jyeshtha–Moola gandanta (Abhukta Mula) is traditionally considered the most intense of the three junctions.

grahan_dosha.name: Grahan (Eclipse) Dosha
grahan_dosha.rule: Sun or Moon in the same sign as Rahu or Ketu; severity graded by orb (<5° strong, <10° moderate, else mild).

source_refs.detail: Same-sign conjunction definition with orb grading follows the common software convention; classical texts grade by eclipse proximity at birth

grahan_dosha.practitioner_explanation: Checks whether the Sun or Moon shares a sign with Rahu or Ketu, then grades severity purely by the orb between the luminary and the node — this is a same-sign proxy, not a check against actual eclipse ephemeris.
grahan_dosha.lay_explanation: The Sun or Moon in your chart sits close to one of the lunar nodes — a combination some traditions associate with an eclipse-adjacent influence.
grahan_dosha.strength_rubric: severity by orb between luminary and node: <5° strong, <10° moderate, else mild (same sign but wide).
caveats: Same-sign definition with orb grading is a software convention; classical texts more strictly require birth near an actual eclipse.
Not evaluated against real eclipse ephemeris data — this is a same-sign proxy, not eclipse detection.
notes: Orb thresholds are convention-dependent; some traditions require birth near an actual eclipse rather than any luminary-node conjunction.
